An Report 
On 
SUMMER VACATION ACADEMIC COURSE 
Submitted to Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli for the partial fulfillment 
of Bachelor of Engineering (UG) Degree in Information Technology 
 
Submitted By 
 
 
Adarsh Tanaji Patil   246109067 
 
Course: B.Tech (IT) - Third Year         
Course Duration: 01/06/2026 to 14/07/2026 
Guided By 
Dr. A. J. Umbarkar 
 
 
 
 
 
Department of Information Technology 
Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli 
 
Academic Year 2026 – 27 (Sem-V) 

ACKNOWLEDGEMENT 
 
 
 
I would like to express my sincere gratitude to everyone who supported and encouraged me throughout 
my Summer Self-Learning Program. This program provided me with an opportunity to independently 
enhance my technical knowledge and gain practical experience beyond my regular academic curriculum. 
During this program, I completed self-learning courses in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning 
(AI/ML), SQL and Database Management, and Docker & Kubernetes. I am grateful to the various 
online learning resources, tutorials, and technical documentation that helped me understand and 
practically apply the concepts covered in these courses. 
Finally, I would like to thank my family and friends for their continuous moral support and 
encouragement throughout this learning journey.

1. Abstract: 
 
a. Completed a 5-week self-driven learning program during the summer vacation. 
b. Focused on strengthening practical, industry-relevant technical skills outside regular 
coursework. 
c. Covered three areas: Docker & Kubernetes, Artificial Intelligence & Machine 
Learning (AIML), and SQL. 
d. Gained hands-on experience with containerization, orchestration, machine learning 
workflows, and relational database management. 
e. Practiced concepts through hands-on labs, coding exercises, and mini-tasks in each 
area. 
f. Achieved improved technical proficiency, logical thinking, and overall readiness 
across DevOps, AI/ML, and database domains. 
 
 
2. Introduction: 
 
2.1 Objective of the Course - 
 
a. To gain hands-on exposure to containerization and orchestration using Docker and 
Kubernetes. 
b. To build a working understanding of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning 
concepts and tools. 
c. To strengthen database design and query skills using SQL. 
d. To bridge theoretical coursework with practical, industry-relevant tools and workflows. 
e. To build a strong technical foundation for future projects, internships, and placements. 
 
 
5 

2.2 Importance of the Course - 
 
a. Bridges the gap between theoretical learning and practical application. 
b. Covers widely-used industry tools for deployment (Docker/Kubernetes), data-driven 
decision making (AIML), and data management (SQL). 
c. Encourages continuous learning through structured, hands-on practice. 
d. Builds a strong, well-rounded foundation for software development and data-oriented 
roles. 
e. Enhances problem-solving, analytical thinking, and technical confidence. 
 
 
3. About the Organization: 
a. Docker & Kubernetes: Completed through Red Hat learning resources, focusing on 
containerization and container orchestration. 
b. Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning (AI/ML): Learning through Apna College, 
covering fundamental AI/ML concepts and practical applications. 
c. SQL & MySQL: Learned through YouTube-based tutorials, focusing on SQL queries, 
database management, and MySQL. 
d. The courses were completed independently through online learning resources during 
the summer vacation. 
e. The learning activities included theoretical study, practical exercises, coding practice, 
and hands-on implementation. 
 
 
4. Course Work Description: 
 
3.1 Module 1 – Docker & Kubernetes (1 July to 14 July) - 
❖ Introduction to containerization concepts and comparison with traditional virtual machines. 
❖ Installed Docker and practiced building custom images using Dockerfiles. 
❖ Worked with Docker commands – build, run, exec, ps, logs, volumes, and networks. 
❖ Used Docker Compose to define and run multi-container applications. 
❖ Learned Kubernetes architecture – Pods, Nodes, ReplicaSets, and Deployments. 
❖ Practiced deploying and scaling applications using kubectl and minikube. 
❖ Explored Kubernetes Services, ConfigMaps, and Secrets for configuration management. 
❖ Understood load balancing, rolling updates, and self-healing in Kubernetes clusters. 
 
6 

3.2 Module 2 – Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning - 
❖ Revisited Python fundamentals with a focus on NumPy and Pandas for data handling. 
❖ Performed data cleaning, preprocessing, and exploratory data analysis (EDA). 
❖ Visualized datasets using Matplotlib and Seaborn. 
❖ Explored unsupervised learning concepts such as K-Means clustering. 
❖ Got an introductory overview of neural networks and deep learning concepts. 
 
3.3 Module 3 – SQL & Database Management - 
❖ Studied core DBMS concepts – tables, keys, relationships, and normalization. 
❖ Practiced DDL commands – CREATE, ALTER, DROP for schema design. 
❖ Practiced DML commands – SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE for data 
manipulation. 
❖ Wrote queries using JOINs (INNER, LEFT, RIGHT), subqueries, and aggregate functions. 
❖ Applied GROUP BY, HAVING, and ORDER BY clauses for data summarization. 
❖ Learned about indexes, constraints, and basic query optimization. 
❖ Practiced writing simple stored procedures and views using MySQL. 
 
 
 
 
5. Course Experience: 
 
a. The learning program was self-paced and carried out during the summer vacation. 
b. Followed a systematic weekly schedule moving from containerization tools to AIML and 
finally SQL. 
c. Practiced through hands-on lab environments for containerization, model building, and query 
writing. 
d. Improved problem-solving ability, technical confidence, and cross-domain understanding. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
7 

6. Tools and Technologies Used: 
 
❖ Docker – for building, packaging, and running containerized applications. 
❖ Kubernetes (kubectl, minikube) – for container orchestration, scaling, and 
deployment. 
❖ Python (NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib) – for data analysis and machine learning. 
❖ SQL (MySQL) – for database design, querying, and data management. 
❖ Text Editor / IDE (VS Code) – for writing and testing code and configuration files. 
❖ Computer System & Internet – for accessing learning material and practicing labs. 
 
 
 
8 

7. Learning Outcomes: 
 
a. Developed a practical understanding of containerization and orchestration using Docker 
and Kubernetes. 
b. Gained hands-on experience in building and evaluating basic machine learning models. 
c. Strengthened database design and SQL querying skills. 
d. Improved analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities through cross-domain practice. 
e. Gained exposure to industry-relevant tools used in DevOps, AI/ML, and data management 
roles. 
 
 
 
 
8. Conclusion: 
 
This self-driven summer learning program was a highly enriching and productive experience. 
Over five weeks, I completed structured, hands-on modules covering Docker & Kubernetes, 
Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning, and SQL. The program provided practical exposure 
to containerization and orchestration, machine learning workflows, and relational database 
management through guided exercises and mini-tasks. 
This experience significantly enhanced my technical proficiency, logical thinking, and 
problem-solving abilities across three important and widely-used domains in the software 
industry. Overall, this program has contributed greatly to my personal and academic 
development and has strengthened my foundation for future projects, internships, and 
placements. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Dr. A. J. Umbarkar Ms. J. J. Mujawar Dr. U. B. Chavan 
Guide/Mentor Internship Coordinator Head
